line-hi.note: Raised from 0.42 on 2026-07-28. At 0.42 it measured 2.27:1 and failed WCAG 1.4.11's 3:1 non-text floor while carrying the today-ring state. Now 3.33:1.

wordmark.purpose: Archivo Black, lowercase 'uptime'. Appears exactly once per screen, in the header. Never used for anything else.

display.purpose: The uptime metric only. One per screen, ever. Monospaced and tabular so it cannot jitter as it counts.

label.purpose: The connective vocabulary of the product — status pills, captions, lever names, metric subtitles. Uppercase, tracked out.

motion.name: ease-out-quart
motion.purpose: The system's only easing curve. Decisive out, no overshoot.

motion.name: state-change
motion.purpose: Default for any state transition — press, log, recede.

motion.name: grid-fill
motion.purpose: A day cell filling when its day goes up. The one moment allowed to be slower than a press.

motion.name: nav-pending-delay
motion.purpose: A pending-navigation indicator fades in only after this delay, so a fast transition never flashes one.

breakpoints.name: column
breakpoints.purpose: The single column's max width. There is no second breakpoint — the product does not gain a column on a large display.

components.name: Lever Button
components.description: The primary action of the entire product. One tap logs the day. Sized as the most important control on screen.
components.css: .ds-lever { display: block; width: 100%; min-height: 64px; padding: 20px 16px; background: #1e2226; color: #eceff1; border: 1px solid #61676d; border-radius: 4px; font-family: Inter, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 0.8125rem; font-weight: 500; letter-spacing: 0.08em; text-transform: uppercase; cursor: pointer; transition: background 150ms cubic-bezier(0.25,1,0.5,1); } .ds-lever:hover { background: #2c3136; } .ds-lever:active { background: #61676d; } .ds-lever:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #b4b8bc; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Lever Button — logged
components.description: State is shown by recession, never by a success colour. The control becomes non-interactive.
components.css: .ds-lever-done { display: block; width: 100%; min-height: 64px; padding: 20px 16px; background: #15191c; color: #858a8f; border: 1px solid #2c3136; border-radius: 4px; font-family: Inter, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 0.8125rem; font-weight: 500; letter-spacing: 0.08em; text-transform: uppercase; cursor: default; }

components.name: Day Grid
components.description: The signature component. 15 cells per row, 3px apart. Fill intensity encodes how many levers fired, never which. Down cells carry a border so state never rests on fill alone.
components.css: .ds-grid { display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(15, minmax(0, 1fr)); gap: 3px; list-style: none; margin: 0; padding: 0; max-width: 320px; } .ds-grid li { aspect-ratio: 1; border-radius: 1px; transition: background 200ms cubic-bezier(0.25,1,0.5,1); } .ds-grid .up-multi { background: #eceff1; } .ds-grid .up { background: #b4b8bc; } .ds-grid .down { background: #15191c; border: 1px solid #2c3136; } .ds-grid .today { background: #15191c; border: 1px solid #2c3136; box-shadow: 0 0 0 1px #0d1013, 0 0 0 2px #61676d; }

components.name: Status Pill
components.description: UP is muted and colourless — the absence of alarm is the signal. DEGRADED is the only variant that takes a hue.
components.css: .ds-pill-up, .ds-pill-degraded { font-family: Inter, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 0.6875rem; font-weight: 500; letter-spacing: 0.08em; text-transform: uppercase; } .ds-pill-up { color: #858a8f; } .ds-pill-degraded { color: #f2ab35; }

components.name: Playbook Chip
components.description: A one-tap shortcut to a detail that worked before. Actions, not filters — there is no selected state.
components.css: .ds-chip { display: block; width: 100%; text-align: left; min-height: 44px; padding: 12px 16px; background: #1e2226; color: #eceff1; border: 1px solid #2c3136; border-radius: 4px; font-family: Inter, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 0.9375rem; cursor: pointer; transition: background 150ms cubic-bezier(0.25,1,0.5,1); } .ds-chip:hover { background: #2c3136; } .ds-chip:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #b4b8bc; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Input
components.description: 16px minimum on touch, because iOS force-zooms any focused field below that.
components.css: .ds-input { display: block; width: 100%; min-height: 44px; padding: 12px; background: #15191c; color: #eceff1; border: 1px solid #2c3136; border-radius: 4px; font-family: Inter, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; } .ds-input::placeholder { color: #858a8f; } .ds-input:focus { border-color: #61676d; outline: 2px solid #b4b8bc; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Navigation
components.description: Label-scale links, muted at rest, readout white when active. On native this is replaced by the platform's own tab bar or navigation bar, themed with these colours rather than reimplemented.
components.html: historyproofplaybooksettings
components.css: .ds-nav { display: flex; border-top: 1px solid #2c3136; } .ds-nav a { flex: 1; padding: 16px 8px; text-align: center; color: #858a8f; text-decoration: none; font-family: Inter, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 0.6875rem; font-weight: 500; letter-spacing: 0.08em; text-transform: uppercase; transition: color 150ms cubic-bezier(0.25,1,0.5,1); } .ds-nav a.active { color: #eceff1; } .ds-nav a:hover { color: #b4b8bc; }

narrative.overview: A readout for a system that is either up or it isn't. It borrows from status pages, monitoring dashboards, and equipment panels: a dominant numeric readout, a dense state grid, flat unlit surfaces, and status colour that appears only when something is wrong. The governing move is restraint as signal — UP has no colour at all, because the absence of an alarm IS the information. Amber and red are the only saturated values in the system and they are never decorative. Every surface is flat; there is not one shadow in the product. Depth comes from tonal layering across five near-black steps, the way a physical panel is separated by material rather than by lighting. The palette is committed dark, and this is not a theme choice — the product is opened at 6am and at 11pm, and a white screen at either hour is hostile.
keyCharacteristics: Flat by absolute rule — zero shadows, depth by tonal step only
One dominant numeric readout per screen, at a scale nothing else approaches
Colour reserved exclusively for degraded and down states
Monospaced tabular numerals everywhere a number can change
Uppercase, tracked-out micro-labels as the connective vocabulary
Single narrow column, phone-first, at every viewport

rules.name: The Quiet-Is-Good Rule
rules.body: UP gets no colour. Status colour exists only to mark degraded and down. Giving the healthy state its own hue would make the absence of alarm indistinguishable from the presence of one at a glance, which is the entire job of the panel.

rules.name: The Two-Hue Ceiling
rules.body: Amber and red are the only saturated hues the system owns. No third status colour, no accent, no category colours for levers. Colour is reserved for status, never for identity.

rules.name: The Measured-Not-Assumed Rule
rules.body: The web source is normative in oklch; the hex is its exact sRGB rendering and is what React Native consumes, since RN cannot parse oklch. When any value changes, re-measure the contrast rather than assuming it held.

rules.name: The One Readout Rule
rules.body: Exactly one element per screen is set at Display scale, and it is always the number that answers the screen's question. If a second element competes with it, the screen has two subjects and needs splitting.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: Every numeral that can change is monospaced and set with tabular figures. A number that reflows as it counts reads as unstable, and this product's whole claim is that the readout is trustworthy.

rules.name: The Scalable-Type Rule
rules.body: On native the ramp maps onto Dynamic Type and sp units, never hard-coded points. The exception is Display: the hero metric is capped so it cannot overflow, and degrades by reducing its own size before it wraps. A wrapped hero metric is a broken screen.

rules.name: The No-Cast Rule
rules.body: A surface that needs to feel raised gets the next tonal step. If three steps are not enough separation, the layout is too dense — fix the spacing, not the lighting. Glassmorphism, blur, glow, and drop shadows are all outside the system.

dos: Do reserve amber (#f2ab35) and red (#f05653) exclusively for degraded and down states.
Do set every changeable numeral in JetBrains Mono with tabular figures.
Do convey elevation with the next tonal step (#0d1013 -> #15191c -> #1e2226).
Do keep exactly one Display-scale element per screen.
Do map the type ramp onto Dynamic Type and sp on native so text follows the user's reading-size setting.
Do re-measure contrast whenever a colour value changes; the ratios are measured, not estimated.
Do hold the single 28rem column at every viewport.
donts: Don't add a shadow. Anywhere. At any elevation.
Don't give the healthy state a colour — quiet is the signal.
Don't colour-code levers, or introduce a third status hue.
Don't use a status colour decoratively: not on a border, an icon, or a heading that isn't reporting a state.
Don't hard-code point sizes on native, or let the hero metric wrap.
Don't introduce a light theme, a theme toggle, gradients, blur, or glow.
Don't mark a logged lever with a green or 'success' treatment; it recedes instead.
Don't let a native default (Material's shadow elevation, an iOS grouped list's own background) reintroduce a surface this system doesn't have.
